1. Introduction
The purpose of this policy is to set out South East Technological University’s (SETU) 
commitment to the principles and promotion of supporting caring employees in all 
aspects of institutional activity and to detail how this policy will be implemented. It is 
important to SETU that employees who care for individuals who are in need of 
personal care or support due to serious medical condition, illness, disability or frailty 
are supported. SETU recognises that a supportive employer responds flexibly and can 
support employees who are caring to identify ways to balance work, their career and 
care.  As highlighted further in Appendix 1, the number of people with caring 
responsibilities in Ireland continues to grow, making workplace support increasingly 
important. 
SETU is committed to ensuring that employees who undertake caregiving—including 
those with advocacy or legal responsibilities such as acting under an Enduring Power 
of Attorney (EPA)—are supported in balancing their work, career and care 
commitments. 
SETU is an equal opportunities employer and as per its Equality, Diversity and 
Inclusion (EDI)Policy and Section.42 Public Sector Duty5, is committed to the 
continued development of employment policies, procedures and practices which 
prevent discrimination on the specified statutory grounds of gender, civil status, family 
status, ethnicity, age, disability, sexual orientation, religion or membership of the 
Travelling community along with socio economic status.  
The intention of this policy is to highlight these supports and policies in one place for 
ease of access and provide guidance for employees.  
1.2 Legal Framework  
This policy is informed by the Employment Equality Acts 1998-2015 and the Equal 
Status Acts 2000-2018 which prohibit direct and indirect discrimination, sexual 
harassment, harassment and victimisation in relation to nine specified equality 
grounds: gender, family status, civil status, sexual orientation, age, disability, religion, 
ethnicity and membership of the Traveller community. The Employment Equality Acts 
prohibit discrimination

in employment, including recruitment, promotion, pay and other conditions of 
employment. The Equal Status Acts prohibit discrimination in access to and provision 
of services, accommodation and educational establishments.  The Irish Human Rights 
and Equality Commission Act 2014 s. 42, requires that in the performance of their 
functions public bodies shall have regard to the need to eliminate discrimination, 
promote equality of opportunity and treatment and protect the human rights of staff 
and service users.   
The Work Life Balance and Miscellaneous Provisions Act 2023 introduced several 
measures aimed at enhancing employees' work-life balance and supporting those with 
caregiving responsibilities.   
This policy reflects SETU’s  commitment to honour its obligations under these Acts.  
1.3  Scope of Policy 
This policy applies to all SETU employees and governs decisions related to 
recruitment, selection, promotion, access to training, and terms and conditions of 
employment. 
1.4 Definitions 
For the purposes of this policy, the following definitions apply: 
Carer / Caring Employee 
An employee who provides ongoing or intermittent personal care, support, or 
assistance to an individual who requires it due to disability, long-term illness, frailty, or 
a serious medical condition. Caring responsibilities may include practical, emotional, 
medical, supervisory or advocacy support. 
Prescribed Dependent / Person Being Cared For 
A person for whom the employee provides care and who meets the criteria defined in 
relevant legislation (including the Work Life Balance and Miscellaneous Provisions Act 
2023, Carer’s Leave Act 2001 and associated guidance). This may include a child, 
spouse, civil partner, cohabitant, sibling, parent, grandparent, or a person who resides 
with the employee in a relationship of domestic dependency.

Supporting Employees with Caring Responsibilities Policy Version 1.0 
Page 6 of 22 
Carer Passport 
A voluntary and confidential document jointly agreed between an employee and their 
line manager, which captures the accommodations, flexibilities, and supports needed 
to enable an employee to balance work with caring responsibilities. The Carer 
Passport facilitates open communication, consistency, and continuity of support and is 
transferred between managers if reporting lines change.
Advocacy Roles 
Advocacy refers to supporting a prescribed dependent in navigating services, 
decision-making or care systems and may include communicating with health, social 
care, legal or educational services on their behalf. 
Enduring Power of Attorney (EPA) 
A legally recognised arrangement under Irish law enabling an appointed individual (the 
attorney) to make decisions on behalf of another person who lacks or may lose 
capacity. Where an employee is acting in an advocacy role such as under an EPA, the 
University recognises these responsibilities as part of their caring role where duties 
support the care or wellbeing of a prescribed dependent. 
2. 
Principles
•
SETU is committed to supporting caring employees in all aspects of 
University activity.
•
SETU is committed to working to understand the evolving needs of caring 
employees.
•
SETU is committed to responding flexibly and sensitively to employees who 
are caring to identify ways to balance work, their career and care.
2.1  Other policies 
This policy should be read in conjunction with additional relevant SETU policies 
and procedures (See section 3.1 and 3.2).

3. 
Balancing work and caring responsibilities
SETU acknowledges that the experiences of caregivers can differ widely, and that the 
kind of support needed may evolve over time. As a care giver, you are invited to 
discuss with your line manager your life as a carer and about how SETU and your 
manager can support you most effectively. 
These discussions can explore flexible working arrangements, leave options, 
workload management, and opportunities for career development. Employees are 
invited to approach these conversations thoughtfully, considering both immediate and 
longer-term support needs, and to maintain ongoing communication as 
circumstances evolve.  
Appendix 2 offers guidance to consider in advance of employee-manager meetings 
which will guide conversations around flexibility, leave, and balancing work and 
caregiving obligations.   
3.1 
Carer Friendly Policies 
Carer Friendly Policies help employees balance work and caring responsibilities, 
supporting them to fulfil both effectively. SETU provides a range of internal flexible 
working and leave options, including core meeting hours, hybrid working, job sharing, 
shorter working year and career breaks, alongside statutory leave options such as 
force majeure, leave for medical care purposes, carers leave, and domestic violence 
leave. A brief summary of the list of policies can be found in Appendix 3, with further 
information available on the HR Policies SharePoint. 
3.2 Overview of Flexible Working Options 
Core Meeting Hours Guidelines.  
Core meeting hours are from 10.00 AM to 4:00 PM, Monday to Friday. These hours 
are a subset of the working day, not a representation of its full duration. Meetings 
encompass all University and faculty level gatherings, including seminars and 
workshops, where employees are required or invited to participate. However, they do 
not include scheduled teaching or assessments.

Hybrid Working 
Hybrid working is a flexible work model that combines remote and in-office work, 
allowing employees to split their time between home and the workplace. It 
offers greater flexibility while maintaining collaboration and productivity.  Hybrid 
working is available to eligible Professional, Managerial, and Support Staff (PMSS) 
who can apply for hybrid working in line with the approved policy. 
Job Sharing 
Job sharing allows two employees to share the responsibilities of a single role, with 
each participant working an agreed portion of the hours. Each job-sharer receives a 
pro-rata salary and associated terms and conditions corresponding to the hours 
worked. Arrangements should be agreed with management and comply with SETU’s 
Job Sharing Policy.  
Shorter Working Year  
The Shorter Working Year scheme enables Professional, Managerial, and Support 
(PMSS) Staff to take unpaid leave of up to 13 weeks with the possibility of spreading 
the reduced salary over a 12-month period.  
3.3 Overview of Leave Options 
Force Majeure 
An employee is entitled to leave with pay for urgent family reasons, for example, an 
injury or illness of a prescribed person where the immediate presence of the employee 
at the place where the person is, whether at their home or elsewhere, is indispensable.  
Duration of Leave: Employees are entitled to up to 3 days in any period of 12 
consecutive months or 5 days in any period of 36 consecutive months. 
Force Majeure leave only relates to a situation which is not foreseeable or otherwise 
not generally predictable. Routine minor and predictable illnesses to children or other 
family members which invariably occur are not covered.

Medical Leave 
Medical Care Leave offers short-term unpaid leave for employees to provide personal 
care or support to a prescribed individual requiring significant assistance due to a 
serious medical condition. This leave is designed to be flexible, allowing parents or 
caregivers to take time off for both unexpected situations and, in some cases, pre-
planned needs.  
Duration of Leave: The entitlement to Medical Care leave extends to 5 working days in 
any period of 12 consecutive months. The minimum leave taken at a time is 1 day. Half 
or part days are counted as 1 full day in terms of total entitlement.  
Prescribed person (as described in the Work Life Balance Miscellaneous Provisions 
Act, 2023) Medical Care leave is granted to one of the following prescribed persons.  
(a)
a person of whom the employee is the relevant parent or acting in loco parentis,
(b)
the spouse, civil partner or cohabitant of the employee,
(c)
a parent or grandparent of the employee,
(d)
a brother, sister or sibling of the employee,
(e)
a person other than one specified in any of paragraphs (a) to (d), who lives in the 
same household as the employee and in need of significant care or support for 
serious medical reasons.
Carers Leave  
Carer’s Leave provides for the temporary absence from work to allow an employee to 
provide full-time care and attention to a person who has been

Supporting Employees with Caring Responsibilities Policy Version 1.0 
Page 10 of 22 
assessed as requiring such support. The employee’s position is protected for the 
duration of the leave, which is unpaid by SETU. 
Eligibility: To qualify, an employee must have at least 12 months’ continuous 
service with SETU and must intend to personally provide full-time care to the 
relevant person. The need for full-time care is determined by a Deciding Officer 
of the Department of Social Protection (DSP), based on medical evidence 
submitted as part of the statutory assessment process. 
Duration: Carer’s Leave may be taken for a minimum of 13 weeks and up to a 
maximum of 104 weeks for each prescribed person. Leave may be taken as 
one continuous period or in shorter, agreed blocks that total up to 104 weeks. 
Where leave is taken in separate blocks, a minimum gap of six weeks must 
occur between each period. In exceptional circumstances, leave of less than 13 
weeks may be approved with the agreement of the employee’s manager. 
Financial Supports: While Carer’s Leave itself is unpaid, employees may be 
eligible to apply for Carer’s Benefit or, where PRSI conditions are not met, a 
means-tested Carer’s Allowance, both administered by the DSP. 
Domestic Violence Leave 
Provides for the temporary absence from employment of employees for the purpose of 
dealing with issues arising from domestic violence, while protecting the employee’s 
employment rights. Domestic Violence Leave is paid at the employee’s normal rate of 
pay, and your role is kept open for when you return. Employees do not need to have a 
specific PRSI contribution record to qualify.  
Duration of Leave: Employees are entitled to up to 5 days of paid leave in any period 
of 12 consecutive months. The leave can be taken as a single continuous period or as 
separate days, depending on the employee’s needs. 
Career Break  
A career break is a period of unpaid leave with a maximum duration of 5 years 
reviewed on an annual basis. To be eligible, employees must have satisfactorily 
completed 12 months of service and have at least 12 months

remaining on their contract from the cessation of the approved period of the career 
break.   
3.4 Additional Supports  
Carer Passport  
My Passport (Appendix 4) has been designed to support constructive discussions 
between SETU employees and their managers about the accommodations and 
flexibilities needed to balance work with caring responsibilities. The outcomes of 
these discussions are documented in My Passport, ensuring that agreed supports 
follow the employee throughout their career, providing continuity and consistency in 
workplace support.   
Carers Car Parking  
Family Carers can reserve access to a car park space if required if they must leave 
campus during the working day to tend to the person they are caring for. This must be 
arranged in advance of their absence from the workplace with relevant HR and 
estates personnel.    
SETU’s Carers Circle  
The SETU Carer Circle, delivered in partnership with Family Carers Ireland via 
webinar, serves as an online peer-support network for both current and former family 
carers. It provides a safe and confidential space where participants can share 
experiences, challenges and insights related to their caregiving roles, fostering 
connection and mutual support within the SETU community. Further information, is 
available on the SETU website and through regular email communication. 
Employee Assistance Service 
A confidential 24-hour service accessible to all staff through the Employee 
Assistance Service (EAS) SETU | Employee Assistance Service

4. Training
SETU is committed to ensuring that all managers are equipped with the knowledge 
and skills required to effectively support employees with caring responsibilities. To 
uphold the principles of this policy, SETU will provide targeted training for managers 
that promotes awareness of the challenges faced by caring employees, highlights the 
supports available within the University, and develops practical competencies for 
responding sensitively and appropriately to individual needs. 
5. 
Review of Policy
This policy will be reviewed in advance of the review date i.e. day month year, and/or 
as soon as possible following new or updated legislation, national or sectoral policy.  
6. 
Policy Author
The authors of this policy are the Vice President of Equality, Diversity and Inclusion. 
Any feedback or issues arising on implementation of this policy should be 
communicated to the HR Manager who will ensure that the Policy Owner is informed 
of these matters as part of the policy review process.

1. Appendix Context
In Ireland, the number of people who regularly provide unpaid care rose by more 
than 50% between 2016 and 2022, from 195, 263 in 2016 to 299, 128 later. Of the 
carers in 2022, 39% (117,536) were men and 61% (181,592) were women. The age 
group most likely to regularly provide unpaid care in Ireland was those between the 
ages of 50 and 59. As the population ages, it is anticipated that the demand for care 
will soon surpass the supply. Consequently, the act of balancing work with care is 
gaining traction as an important health, social and economic issue6.  Between the 
ages of 30 and 59, the percentage of female carers was greater (68%) than that of 
male carers (63%). The largest proportion of carers (15%) were between the ages of 
50 and 54, followed by 14% in each of the age categories of 45 to 49 and 55 to 597. 
Workers in this age group may also be responsible for dual childcare duties.  “Family 
carers are the principal source of care for those in need of support due to a long-
term illness, disability or frailty in the community8; it is estimated that this group 
saves the Irish economy about €20 billion through their unpaid duties.9”  
“A supportive work environment may be the remedy to some of the negative impacts 
often associated with caregiving, such as poor physical and psychological health, 
financial strain, and in extreme cases, withdrawal from the workforce. Provision 
needs to be made for carers in the workplace to facilitate enhanced outcomes in the 
spheres of their physical health, mental health, employment and work-life balance as 
a whole”10 11.   
In 2024, The SETU Caring Employers Employee Survey Report found that 90.2% of 
153 survey respondents engage in at least one caregiving task

2. Appendix Getting the best from your conversation
Table 1: Getting the best from your conversation 
Prepare 
Meeting with your manager gives you the chance to discuss your options in 
an open and honest manner. Over time, this may change based on the type 
of care you are giving. Before approaching your manager:  
●
Review this guide in conjunction with the relevant policies.
●
Consider what short-, medium- and long-term supports may need to 
be put in place.
●
Talk to other supports such as a member of the HR team, Employee 
Assistance Service) EAS, or trusted colleagues in advance of 
discussions with your line manager if required.
Book a Meeting 
Set up a meeting with your direct line manager.  Setting a time and date in the 
diary allows your manager to prepare for the meeting. 
Request that the meeting takes place in a quiet area free from outside 
interruptions.   
Make a Plan 
Your manager is responsible for supporting you in identifying appropriate 
measures to balance work and caring responsibilities. Together, you can 
agree an action plan that is reasonable, proportionate, and operationally 
feasible. Your manager may require time to seek guidance from HR or to 
confirm the supports and arrangements available under University policy and 
applicable legislation. 
Discuss support:  
•
Flexible Working and Leave Options
-
Discuss flexible working options

You may be asked to complete the appropriate form depending on the type 
of leave or flexible working arrangement you are requesting.
-
Provide as much reasonable notice as possible to your manager when

-
Provide relevant information as required.
• Managing Your Workload
-
Be transparent about workloads. If you need support, you should discuss 
your needs with your manager as soon as is feasible.
• Establish the level of confidentiality with your manager.
-

Follow Up 
Caring often evolves and changes over time. 
●
Maintain open and on-going communication with your manager about 
balancing caring and workload and when flexibility is required. It may be 
that you need to change agreed arrangements if the caring role evolves.
●
Caring responsibilities can, at times, place a burden on individuals. Taking 
time for self-care and minding your mental health and well-being is critical 
for your wellbeing and for the well-being of those you care for. You are 
encouraged to check-in with your line manager about balancing workload 
and caring responsibilities, and to access the Employee Assistance 
Services (EAS) if you feel additional support, guidance, or a confidential 
space to talk would be helpful. Ongoing issues can also be raised through 
the University’s grievance procedure to ensure concerns are addressed 
fairly and transparently.

4. Appendix Carer Passport
 WHAT IS ‘MY PASSPORT’? 
My Passport has been designed to enable SETU employees and their 
managers to discuss what accommodations/flexibilities are needed to 
combine work alongside a caring role at home. The information held 
within this document is private and confidential and has been authorised 
by the employee named below to be held on file within HR. By signing the 
below, you are agreeing to having this personal information kept on file 
(soft/hard copies) until such time as your caring role changes or you 
leave employment.  
The accommodations set out within this passport have been agreed with 
the named employee and line manager. It is the commitment of the 
employer to ensure any agreements are migrated over when a new line 
manager takes over.
